item.title: World’s oldest near-complete Roman armour may reveal a lost soldier’s fate
item.description: Archaeologists conserved an intact Roman armour suit from the Kalkriese battlefield. This armour represents the earliest known lorica segmentata, revealing sophisticated engineering. CT scans helped uncover the armour's hidden structure without causing damage. A Roman restraint found with the armour raises questions about a captured soldier. The discovery provides a rare personal glimpse into a disastrous Roman military campaign.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Qatari Diar lists $64 million London penthouse at redeveloped Chelsea Barracks site
item.description: A new duplex penthouse at London's Chelsea Barracks is now for sale. This luxury property is listed for forty-eight million pounds, making it very expensive. The development transformed a historic British Army barracks into a high-end residential neighborhood. Buyers can move into the fully furnished home which includes extensive outdoor terraces. This listing highlights London's ultra-prime housing market's renewed momentum.

item.title: Washington teenager wins $75,000 after creating sponge to trap salmon-killing tyre pollutant
item.description: An eighteen-year-old student developed a jute waste sponge for pollution control. This innovation removes a toxic tire pollutant harming salmon in waterways. The biodegradable sponge offers a sustainable and low-cost filtration alternative. It effectively filters 6PPD-quinone and other contaminants from water. This project won a major science award for its environmental impact.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Africa is pouring in $50 billion to redirect water from Congo River Basin to Lake Chad which has shrunk by 90% since 1960
item.description: Lake Chad's dramatic shrinkage has brought about severe impacts on the lives of millions. To counteract this crisis, governments are investing in initiatives aimed at rehabilitating the lake's ecosystem. A noteworthy solution includes the ambitious Transaqua project, which seeks to channel water from the Congo River back into Lake Chad. This vital endeavor aims not only to replenish the lake but also to foster economic growth in the surrounding regions.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Twitch Streamer Mitch Jones faces legal threat after recreating $500K Deal or No Deal game show
item.description: Twitch streamer Mitch Jones says he received a cease and desist just days after hosting a real-life version of Deal or No Deal featuring Sodapoppin, Nmplol, and cash prizes worth up to $500,000. According to Mitch, the official production demanded money over the unauthorized recreation of the show's format. No lawsuit has been reported so far, and there has been no public resolution as of July 30.
item.dc:creator: Global Sports Desk

item.title: Inside China's new $517 million natural history museum that takes visitors from the cosmos to human evolution, featuring meteorites, dinosaurs and a river-inspired design
item.description: Shenzhen Natural History Museum opened on July 28, 2026, becoming southern China's first major institution dedicated to natural history. The museum's design draws inspiration from a river delta, creating a flowing, curvilinear structure. Visitors will journey from the cosmos through Earth's history and dinosaur eras and eventually learn about the delicate balance of our natural world.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: An Oklahoma wind farm is creating an invisible river of wind that reaches much higher than scientists once thought
item.description: Scientists mapped wind farm wakes in Oklahoma with detailed observations. The study revealed upward momentum transfer extending far beyond turbine blades. These atmospheric disturbances spread vertically, creating a "river of wind" effect. Low-level jets and gravity waves influenced wake recovery significantly. Findings will improve future wind energy production and farm layout models.

item.title: Japan's 600-year-old Daisugi forestry method lets a single tree produce timber for centuries
item.description: Japan's 600-year-old Daisugi technique offers a unique way to produce timber without cutting down entire trees. Developed in Kyoto during the 14th century, the method allows a single cedar tree to grow multiple straight trunks that can be harvested for centuries. The ancient practice is now drawing attention as an example of sustainable forestry amid growing concerns over global deforestation
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.description: During the RHS Sandringham Flower Show, King Charles embraced the challenges of ageing with humor while discussing his cancer treatment and progress. item.title: Trump invites teen lifeguard Ryder Williams to White House after heroic beach rescue
item.description: President Donald Trump has invited 16-year-old California lifeguard Ryder Williams and his family to the White House after the teenager rescued a young boy from powerful waves at Seabright State Beach. Trump said Williams deserves a high civilian honour for his bravery. The dramatic rescue, captured on video, has drawn widespread praise from officials, witnesses and social media users, with many calling the rookie lifeguard true hero

item.title: 11 police personnel, 15 militants killed in overnight attack in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa
item.description: A major militant attack occurred overnight on a police post in Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. Eleven police personnel and fifteen attackers died during the fierce exchange of gunfire. The Khazina police post in Hangu district was the target of this significant assault. Security forces fought back, killing the militants and repelling the attack. This incident highlights the ongoing rise in militant violence in the region.
